text:
Anya: Heads-up — last two deploys we've seen org-level bursts deplete per-key credits and cause the global request queue to hit ~90% for ~30s. Thinking about a change: instead of hard 429 at token exhaustion, consider a 'grace tokens' approach that lets small bursts enter a short soft-queue (200ms) before rejecting with 503 if overall queue latency exceeds SLO. Thoughts?
Sam: Quick clarifying q — how is this different from our current per-key burst window? sounds like extra queuing that could cause head-of-line blocking.
Miguel: If the soft-queue is tiny it's effectively token-bucket + micro-queue. Concern: 503 signals server overload; clients might retry immediately and make it worse. 429 encourages client-side backoff.
Anya: Agree on the 429 semantics. My thinking: use 429 when a specific key has exhausted its burst allowance (so the client knows to back off). Use 503 only when the whole system is overloaded (queue latency > global threshold) and we must shed regardless of per-key state. So two layers: per-key early 429, global forced 503.
Liz: How do we compute "global queue latency"? avg can oscillate; p95 or p99 might be better. Also need a small cooldown so we don't flip every few seconds.
Raj: From telemetry side we need metrics: per-org burst credits, soft-queue occupancy, enqueue timestamp histogram. Also capture sample traces for shed requests so we can see retry patterns.
Anya: Rough config example (pseudo):
```json
{
  "per_key": {
    "burst_tokens": 20,
    "refill_rate_per_sec": 1
  },
  "soft_queue": {
    "max_latency_ms": 200,
    "max_slots": 500
  },
  "global_shed": {
    "p95_queue_latency_ms": 250,
    "cooldown_s": 30
  }
}
```
routing-bot: feature-flag check: "soft_queue_shedding" is off in prod for now.
Sam: Implementation sketch: admission controller at edge router. Flow: if per-key tokens > 0 -> accept and decrement. If tokens == 0 -> return 429. If per-key tokens >0 but soft-queue is full -> check global p95; if > hard threshold -> respond 503. Also allow tiny soft-queue for burst smoothing before 429.
Miguel: Edge case — streaming requests hold slots much longer. Suggest we treat streams as "long" and either charge extra burst credits up-front or route them to a separate long-request pool to avoid starving short requests.
Anya: Good point. Proposal: mark streaming flag in admission and charge X credits based on expected session length or require dedicated capacity for heavy streaming keys.
Liz: Console UX: surface a "recently-shed" count per key/org with sample traces and a recommended action card (increase reserved capacity, add client jitter, or contact sales). Also show soft-queue occupancy and p95 latency heatmap.
Raj: +1 on the traces and also emit a shed_reason tag (per_key_exhausted | global_overload | stream_long). Add retry-after header on 429 with recommended backoff window.
Sam: I'll draft a PR for the router admission logic and tests. Any objections to the 503 usage as a global last-resort signal?
Miguel: No objection from me, just document the client implications and update SDKs to include jitter/backoff helpers.
Anya: Thanks — I'll open a short RFC with threshold suggestions and dashboard mockups. @Liz can you take the dashboard mockups?
deploy-bot: RFC created: rdw/infra#3456 — "soft-queue smoothing + two-tier shed (429 per-key, 503 global)"
Sam: Perfect. I'll link the draft PR to the RFC and add unit tests that simulate streaming-heavy and bursty traffic.
Anya: Great, let's sync next week if needed. :thumbsup:
